Le fratture dell'omero prossimale si des: Proximal humerus fractures are described by fragments (head, greater tuberosity, lesser tuberosity, shaft) according to Neer, a fragment being considered displaced beyond 1 cm or 45°. The greater tuberosity is often fractured together with an anterior dislocation, or alone after a fall: upward displacement of even a few millimeters can cause impingement under the acromion. With a single AP view, dislocation (especially posterior) cannot be excluded: an axillary or Y view is needed, and in complex cases CT.
